color-backgrounds-and-typography.label: Color, Backgrounds, and Typography
color-backgrounds-and-typography.summary: Build readable visual hierarchy with foreground and background colors, font families, type scale, weight, line height, and alignment.

try_color_backgrounds_and_typography_ske.title: Try it yourself: Establish a site-wide color and type foundation
try_color_backgrounds_and_typography_ske.prompt:
**Problem**

The pages now have a few targeted rules, but the site still lacks consistent base colors and typography. A shared page foundation should come from one broad rule instead of repeating defaults on many elements.

**Task**

Keep all previous CSS and add a `body` rule with `background-color: #f8fafc`, `color: #1e293b`, and `font-family: Arial, sans-serif`.

try_color_backgrounds_and_typography_ske.title: Try it yourself: Give section headings a stronger foreground color
try_color_backgrounds_and_typography_ske.prompt:
**Problem**

Section headings need to stand out consistently from ordinary text on several pages.

**Task**

Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `h2 { color: #0f172a; }`.

try_color_backgrounds_and_typography_ske.title: Try it yourself: Improve paragraph readability
try_color_backgrounds_and_typography_ske.prompt:
**Problem**

Longer paragraphs on About and Projects are harder to scan when lines sit too close together.

**Task**

Extend the existing `p` rule by adding `line-height: 1.6;` instead of creating a second paragraph rule.

foreground-choice.title: Choose the text-color property
foreground-choice.hint: Think about which declaration changes the visible text itself rather than the area behind it.

help.concept: CSS has separate declarations for the appearance of text and for the surface behind an element.
help.hint_1: Focus on the declaration that affects the letters you read.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that changes the visible text without changing the surrounding surface.

background-choice.title: Choose site-wide typography and readability decisions
background-choice.prompt: Which CSS decisions support a consistent, readable visual system across the portfolio? Select all that apply.
background-choice.hint: Look for choices that create reusable defaults or improve text rhythm without forcing content into arbitrary dimensions.

help.concept: Good typography combines shared defaults with readable spacing while remaining flexible for real content.
help.hint_1: Site-wide defaults belong on a broad shared ancestor; line height controls spacing between lines.
help.hint_2: Duplicated inline presentation and fixed text heights work against reuse and flexible content.

options.a: Use body for broad foreground, background, and font defaults that can be shared by the page.
options.b: Use line-height on paragraphs to improve vertical reading rhythm without changing the text.
options.c: Give every h2 a separate inline color so each page owns an unrelated heading style.
options.d: Force paragraphs to a fixed height so all text blocks occupy exactly the same vertical space.

type-hierarchy-multi.title: Identify typography controls
type-hierarchy-multi.prompt: Which properties can directly contribute to a text hierarchy?
type-hierarchy-multi.hint: Choose CSS properties that affect the visual treatment of text.

help.concept: Size, weight, and family are typography controls.
help.hint_1: Choose CSS properties that affect the visual treatment of text.
help.hint_2: Select every choice that matches the lesson, not just one.

typography-plan-order.title: Order a basic typography plan
typography-plan-order.prompt: Arrange these decisions from broad defaults to targeted emphasis.
typography-plan-order.hint: Start with page-wide defaults before heading emphasis.

help.concept: A consistent typography system begins with defaults and adds deliberate hierarchy.
help.hint_1: Start with page-wide defaults before heading emphasis.
help.hint_2: Follow the sequence from targeting an element to seeing the browser render it.

line-height-fill.title: Name the reading-rhythm property
line-height-fill.prompt: Choose the property that controls spacing between lines of text.
line-height-fill.hint: Think about the declaration that controls vertical breathing room between lines of text.

help.concept: Readable typography depends not only on typeface and size but also on the vertical rhythm between lines.
help.hint_1: This setting affects spacing from one line of text to the next.
help.hint_2: Choose the typography property concerned with vertical line spacing, not font size or alignment.

line-height-fill.template: [blank1] controls the vertical distance between lines within text.

font-weight-fill.title: Choose the typography control
font-weight-fill.prompt: Complete the statement about emphasizing text with CSS.
font-weight-fill.hint: Think about the typography setting that changes how heavy the letter strokes appear.

help.concept: Typography includes independent controls for typeface, size, emphasis, spacing, and alignment.
help.hint_1: This setting changes visual emphasis without changing the text content.
help.hint_2: Choose the property concerned with stroke heaviness rather than size, spacing, or alignment.

font-weight-fill.template: To control how bold text appears, use the [blank1] property.

try-color-backgrounds-and-typography-ske.title: Establish a site-wide color and type foundation
try-color-backgrounds-and-typography-ske.prompt:
**Problem**

The pages now have a few targeted rules, but the site still lacks consistent base colors and typography. A shared page foundation should come from one broad rule instead of repeating defaults on many elements.

**Task**

Keep all previous CSS and add a `body` rule with `background-color: #f8fafc`, `color: #1e293b`, and `font-family: Arial, sans-serif`.
try-color-backgrounds-and-typography-ske.hint: Use one body rule for the site-wide `background`, foreground, and font foundation.

help.concept: A body rule establishes broad inherited `color` and font choices from one site-wide foundation.
help.hint_1: Use one body rule for the site-wide `background`, foreground, and font foundation.
help.hint_2: Compare several pages: the canvas should become softly tinted, default text should darken, and the typography should use the same sans-serif family.
